summary.headline: A fast-growing retailer and lender earning 40% on equity, but on borrowed money; the price assumes that lasts, so it is well above value
summary.text:
Singer (Sri Lanka) PLC (SINS.N0000), the Hayleys-controlled seller of home appliances, electronics, furniture, sewing machines and now motorcycles, mostly on credit, had a record 2025/26: revenue up 46% and profit up 83%. In the six months to September 2026 revenue rose another 30% and profit to owners 20%, but the September quarter's profit fell 6% as finance costs nearly doubled. At Rs 72.50 the share trades at 3.8x its NAV of Rs 19.23 and 10.7x the last 12 months' EPS of Rs 6.78.

The high return on equity (about 40%) comes with net debt of about 4x equity, and the business uses cash rather than producing it, because customer credit and stock grow with sales. Profit has collapsed twice since 2019. At a 20% required return, worked out from the beta, the four methods give a fair value of about **Rs 30.20**. I'd buy only up to about **Rs 25.70** and treat under **Rs 22.70** as a strong buy, so not at today's price. The fair value was Rs 42.30 on 10 November; it is lower mainly because the P/E method now uses the P/E those returns justify (5.4x base, against a chosen 9x), the required return is 20% (19% before) and the residual income fade is five years, not ten.

fullText:
Summary: Singer (Sri Lanka) PLC (SINS.N0000) is growing fast but on borrowed money. Revenue rose 46% and profit 83% in 2025/26, and another 30% and 20% in the six months to September 2026, but the September quarter's profit fell 6% as finance costs nearly doubled. At Rs 72.50 the share trades at 3.8x its NAV of Rs 19.23 and 10.7x trailing EPS of Rs 6.78. Return on equity is about 40%, but net debt is about 4x equity and the business uses cash as customer credit grows. At a 20% required return the fair value is about Rs 30.20 (Rs 42.30 on 10 November). I'd buy only up to about Rs 25.70 and treat under Rs 22.70 as a strong buy. Category 3 (avoid for now), unchanged: it passes 1 of the 4 business tests.

What the business is
Singer sells home appliances (the biggest line, about a third of sales), digital products, electronics, furniture, sewing machines and, since 2025, Piaggio two- and three-wheelers, through over 420 showrooms, mostly on credit. About 26% of revenue is made in its own four factories. Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC, a licensed finance company it controls, takes public deposits and lends. Hayleys PLC owns 67% directly and about 82% with its subsidiaries.

What's new (six months to 30 September 2026, group, unaudited)
- Revenue Rs 74.4bn (+30%); operating profit Rs 8.51bn (+40%); profit to owners Rs 3.50bn (+20%); EPS Rs 3.00 (Rs 2.51).
- September quarter: revenue +21%, but profit to owners −6% (EPS Rs 1.16 against Rs 1.23). Finance costs +94% and bad-debt charges +51% in the quarter.
- Financial services earned Rs 3.86bn of the half's Rs 8.96bn segment result (+52%). Automobiles and other revenue rose 79%.
- Loans and overdrafts Rs 94.5bn (Rs 82.3bn in March); net debt including leases Rs 92.9bn, 4.1x owners' equity of Rs 22.5bn. Singer Finance's customer deposits rose Rs 11.0bn to Rs 52.3bn.
- Stock rose Rs 7.9bn to Rs 41.7bn and customer credit Rs 12.1bn; operating cash flow −Rs 3.6bn (the half-year report counts the deposits inside operating cash; without them about −Rs 14.6bn).
- Dividends Rs 0.50 and Rs 0.34 declared (Rs 0.84 so far for 2026/27).
- Tax disputes: Rs 1.19bn deemed VAT (2014–15) before the Court of Appeal, and VAT and income tax assessments for 2017–2022 (Rs 1.51bn and Rs 1.38bn including penalties) under appeal; no provisions made.

2025/26 (annual report)
Revenue Rs 128.6bn (+46%), operating profit Rs 14.9bn (+74%), profit Rs 7.66bn (+83%), EPS Rs 6.29, dividends Rs 1.84 (four interims). Assets rose 49% to Rs 182bn, mostly customer credit and stock; operating cash flow was −Rs 41.6bn. Bad-debt charges almost doubled to Rs 1.03bn.

Price
Rs 72.50 (CSE close, 27 November 2026). Traded Rs 66.00–92.50 in April–September 2026; Rs 29.50–101.00 in 2025/26.

Required return
Beta 1.14 (provisional): 57% retail at Damodaran's Retail (Special Lines) beta relevered for Singer's own debt (1.27), 43% finance at the non-bank financial services beta (0.97). Cost of equity 8.24% + 1.14 × 10.28% = 20.0% (bear 21.5%, bull 18.5%). No WACC: most of the debt funds lending, so Singer is valued like a finance company, on equity.

Methods (bear / base / bull, Rs a share)
- Justified price to book: 15.15 / 24.72 / 38.46 (weighted 24.60). NAV × (ROE − g) ÷ (r − g) with long-run ROE 18/24/30%.
- P/E (justified): 25.39 / 35.36 / 48.00 (34.90). EPS to March 2027 Rs 5.80 / 6.60 / 7.20 at 4.4x / 5.4x / 6.7x.
- Residual income: 19.97 / 33.86 / 57.23 (34.37). ROE from 40.3% to 18/24/30% over five years.
- Dividend model: 16.72 / 26.98 / 42.53 (27.01). Rs 1.60 / 1.90 / 2.10 next year, growing 4/8/12%.
Fair value (average of the four) Rs 30.22; buy Rs 25.69 (−15%); strong buy Rs 22.67 (−25%).

Checks
- Growth: dividends assumed to grow 4/8/12% a year; supported growth 28.3% (70.7% kept × 40% ROE). Fine.
- Earnings run-rate: base EPS Rs 6.60 is 2.7% below the Rs 6.78 twelve-month figure; the latest quarter × 4 is only Rs 4.64.
- Ratios: ROE 40% is well above the range a business keeps for long; the base case assumes 24%. Net debt 4.1x equity is far above the 1x test. Long-run growth 5–7% is below the 12.24% bond yield.
- No DCF: operating cash flow is negative every year while credit grows, and dividends are paid from borrowing and deposits.

Business tests (1 of 4)
- Return on equity: pass (40% now; average about 22% over six years, but 1% and −1% in 2022/23 and 2023/24).
- Debt: fail (net debt 4.1x equity).
- Steady profit: fail (loss in 2023/24; September 2026 quarter down 6%).
- Cash: fail (operating cash flow −Rs 13.9bn and −Rs 41.6bn in the last two years).

Management and plans
Management wants growth from new brands and categories (Piaggio, Hikvision, HP, Starlink, Bosch), furniture (a factory is being bought), washing machines and Singer Finance's lending. Sales growth has followed, but the promise of stable leverage hasn't: net debt rose Rs 11.5bn in six months and finance costs are rising faster than profit.

Shareholders
Hayleys controls the company (about 82% with its subsidiaries); the public holds 10.94%. In the September quarter the Lynear Wealth Dynamic Opportunities Fund added 3.69mn shares and Invenco Capital 1.21mn; the Capital Alliance Quantitative Equity Fund sold 0.59mn.

Buy plan (500 shares)
200 shares up to Rs 30.20, 150 up to Rs 25.70, 150 up to Rs 22.70: about Rs 13,300 in all (average Rs 26.60), against Rs 36,250 at today's price. That needs a fall of about 65%. It hasn't been near that this year (low Rs 66.00), but the share was Rs 29.50 in April 2025 and Rs 14.50 in August 2024.

What would change my view
Higher: profit growing again in the December quarter with finance costs under control; net debt falling towards 3x equity; bad debts staying low; ROE holding near 30% through a downturn.
Lower: another fall in quarterly profit; higher interest rates or a weaker rupee; bad debts rising faster than lending; net debt above 4.5x equity; losing the tax cases.

Uncertain
Damodaran's emerging-markets betas couldn't be opened, so the beta uses web-search stand-ins (provisional). The half-year report moves Singer Finance's deposits into operating cash flow, unlike the annual report and the June interim, so operating cash flows aren't on one basis. Working capital change isn't stored as one figure (no subtotal printed).
